bib.title: ARC-AGI-3: A New Challenge for Frontier Agentic Intelligence

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "ARC-AGI-3: A New Challenge for Frontier Agentic Intelligence", ARC Prize Foundation (corporate author; footnote lists the team, including François Chollet, Mike Knoop, Gregory Kamradt, Hunter Henry). Preprint, arXiv:2603.24621v2 [cs.AI], 17 Apr 2026 (title page dated April 20, 2026). No venue is printed. No affiliations are printed beyond "ARC Prize Foundation".

COVERAGE: 23 of 23 pages, 62,277 of 62,277 chars, references included. There are no appendices. Figure bodies were not viewed, only captions and the plot text that extracted.

CLAIMS (ranked)

1. What it is: interactive, turn-based environments with no instructions and no stated goal.
   - Observation is a 64x64 grid with 16 colours; actions are five keys, Undo and a cell click.
   - Sizes: 25 public demo, 55 semi-private, 55 fully private (Table 1, p11).
   - quote: "ARC-AGI-3 inverts this balance. The public set shifts from a training resource to a demonstration interface" (p10)
   - The private set is "intentionally out-of-distribution relative to the public set" (p10).

2. Score is RHAE (Relative Human Action Efficiency).
   - Level score: S = min(1.15, (h/a)^2), where h is the human baseline and a is the AI's action count. Formula as printed: "For an environment with n levels (where n = 5), the weight for level l is w_l = l" (p12).
   - Environment score: the linearly weighted mean of level scores, capped at the weighted fraction of levels completed (4 of 5 levels caps at about 66.7%).
   - Total: the mean over environments.
   - quote: "If the upper-median best human completed a level in only 10 actions, but the AI agent took 100 to complete it, then the AI agent scores (10/100)^2 for that level, which gets reported as 1%." (p11)
   - Only environment actions count; tool calls and reasoning steps do not (p7).
   - Agents are cut off at 5x the human median actions per level (p14).

3. Human baseline.
   - quote: "we recorded 486 unique participants across 414 candidate environments. This resulted in 2,893 total environment attempts." (p18)
   - Collected in person at a San Francisco testing centre from members of the general public, in 90-minute sessions.
   - Pay was $115–$140 plus $5 per environment solved (p17).
   - Each environment had a 20-minute soft limit and a 30-minute hard limit.
   - Participants got one first-contact attempt per environment; level resets were allowed.
   - Low-effort sessions were excluded; the count is not given.

4. "Human-solvable" means at least 2 of 10 people solved it.
   - quote: "Each environment was attempted by 10 people. Only environments that could be fully solved by at least two human participants (independently) were considered" (p16)
   - "Many environments were solved by six or more people" (p16); no distribution is given.
   - The headline "humans can solve 100% of the environments" (p1) rests on this bar.
   - The baseline h is the upper-median completer by action count, "e.g., the 3rd-place finisher among 4 or 5 completions" (p13).

5. Validation.
   - Random play is run for 50,000 and 1,000,000 steps, plus a state-graph analysis.
   - quote: "a random policy should not successfully solve a level more often than 1 in 10,000 times" (p9)
   - The tutorial level is exempt: level 1 of ls20 has a win probability of "exactly 1 in 355" (p10).
   - Novelty test: reject a pair of environments if one program solves both while being at least 50% shorter than the two separate solutions concatenated (p8).
   - Environment names are withheld, and public-set scores are never reported officially.

6. AI results on the semi-private set (Table 2, p16).
   - Scores: Opus 4.6 (Max) 0.50%, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview 0.40%, GPT 5.4 (High) 0.20%, Grok-4.20 0.10%.
   - Setup: no harness, no tools, and one shared system prompt.
   - Cost is given only as "tens of thousands of dollars in API costs" (p14); there are no per-model figures.

7. Harness gains do not transfer.
   - quote: "Opus 4.6 scores 0.0% with no harness and 97.1% with the Duke harness (11), yet in environment BP35, Opus 4.6 scores 0.0% under both configurations." (p15)
   - Setup: harnesses were built on ls20, ft09 and vc33, then tested on the rest of the public set.

8. Contamination of ARC-AGI-1 and 2: Gemini 3 Deep Think used the ARC colour mapping in its reasoning although the prompt never gave it (p4). This is one anecdote.

9. Preview competition (July–August 2025, 3 hidden environments): StochasticGoose, a CNN with reinforcement learning, scored 12.58%; Blind Squirrel scored 6.71% (p20). Both were search-based. The paper does not say whether the preview used the same scoring formula.

LIMITS
- No run counts, seeds, variance or confidence intervals are given for any AI score. Differences of 0.1 to 0.5 points are uninterpretable.
- No per-environment AI results, no levels-completed counts and no per-model cost.
- The baseline rests on small samples: at most 10 people per environment and as few as 2 completers. "100% solvable" does not mean most people solve it.
- No count of how many of the 414 candidates were rejected is stated; 135 shipped.
- No results are reported on the fully private set.
- The private set is unverifiable by outsiders, and the semi-private set carries a conceded "small risk of data leakage" (p10).
- The authors concede the 5x action cutoff "may yield marginally lower reported scores" (p14).
- Community leaderboard scores are self-reported and unverified.
- The model list is a March 2026 snapshot.
- Internal inconsistencies:
  - "at least six levels per environment" (p8) against n = 5 in the formula, while Figures 4 and 8 plot 8 and 7 levels.
  - "upper-median" baseline against "human-baseline median" for the cutoff.
  - 10 testers x 414 environments would exceed the 2,893 attempts reported.

BUILDS ON
- Chollet 2019, "On the Measure of Intelligence".
- Spelke and Kinzler 2007, Core Knowledge.
- Anderson et al. 2018, the SPL metric: "inspired by ... Success weighted by Path Length" (p12).
- Fox et al. 2026, the Duke harness.

CODE: none. The system prompt is verbatim on p16: "You are playing a game. Your goal is to win. Reply with the exact action you want to take. The final action in your reply will be executed next turn. Your entire reply will be carried to the next turn."

FIGURES: Figure 4, p12, "Action progression and RHAE scoring for environment re86". It plots 11 human playthroughs as cumulative actions against level reached, each labelled with its final score (100% down to 2%). It shows at a glance how the squared efficiency and the completion cap punish slow or partial runs, including for humans.

PROBLEMS
- Equations 1–3 extracted garbled; I reconstructed them from the surrounding prose, so check them against the PDF before quoting them as formulas.
- Some words are run together in the extraction.
- Figure cross-references in the text are off by one or two.
- The Figure 7 caption prints "correct" twice.
- No embedded instructions are aimed at the reader; the only imperative text is the quoted system prompt.
